elements.element: Renewal requires mutual written agreement unless every conditional automatic-renewal element below is met.
elements.evidence: Renewal remains automatic ("This Agreement will automatically renew for additional 1-year terms") and the conditional preferred elements are not all satisfied (opt-out is 60 days, not 30; no Vendor reminder). No mutual-written-agreement renewal mechanic was inserted.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, each renewal term is no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: Retained language: "will automatically renew for additional 1-year terms" — each renewal term is 12 months.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer may opt out on no more than 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Inserted sentence requires notice "at least 60 days before the end of the then-current Term"; 60 days exceeds the preferred 30-day maximum.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Vendor must remind Customer at least 60 days before renewal.
elements.evidence: No renewal-reminder obligation on Kubient appears anywhere in the rendered operative language; the insertion imposes duties only on Customer.

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 percent.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: renewal is on the same terms and paragraph 4(a) contains no uplift, re-pricing or unilateral fee-increase mechanic (fees are the revenue share set in each Exhibit), so no cap is required.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer's non-renewal notice window is no more than 60 days.
elements.evidence: Inserted operative sentence: "Customer may elect not to renew this Agreement by giving Kubient written notice of non-renewal at least 60 days before the end of the then-current Term, in which case this Agreement will expire at the end of that Term." The deterministic check reported "number not found" (numeral form), but on substance the window is exactly 60 days, at the fallback ceiling.

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at 5 percent.
elements.evidence: Condition not engaged: automatic renewal is on identical terms with no price-increase or uplift mechanic in paragraph 4(a) or the renewal sentence, so no 5% cap language is needed.

reasons: Fallback is complete: the inserted sentence supplies the missing non-renewal mechanic at exactly 60 days, and the price-cap element is not triggered because renewal carries the existing revenue-share economics with no uplift right.

Preferred is not complete: the opt-out is 60 days rather than 30, and no Vendor renewal reminder (60 days pre-renewal) was added. To reach preferred, change "at least 60 days" to "at least 30 days" and add an express Kubient obligation to notify Customer of the upcoming renewal at least 60 days before the end of the then-current Term.

Minimality holds: one concise inserted sentence, no deletions, no survival tails, expense language or extra procedures; Kubient's 90-day post-Initial-Term right and the 4(b) breach/insolvency mechanics are retained intact. The trailing "in which case this Agreement will expire at the end of that Term" is operative effect, not surplus.

Intent is preserved: the new right is Customer-only, does not shorten Customer's own 90-day exit, and creates no dangling cross-reference or undefined term ("Term" and "Initial Term" are defined in 4(a)).

Drafting nit to tighten (not a defect that blocks the fallback): the retained auto-renew sentence renews "unless earlier terminated pursuant to this Agreement's express provisions," which speaks only to termination. Consider conforming it to read "unless earlier terminated or Customer gives notice of non-renewal as provided below" so the expiry route is unmistakably carved into the renewal trigger.
Position note for negotiation: 60 days is the fallback ceiling — do not concede any longer window, and 90+ days would be walk-away.
